correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact block form, simultaneous binary eigenspace splitting, the shear stabilizer dimension, orbit-stabilizer factor, joint ranks, Stirling inversion, and both directions of the maximal-clique characterization. For n>=2 each rank-one quotient projection has zero W-action; commuting with them kills every central block of an additional endomorphism. Direct full-algebra finite-field enumeration verified arities 1--3 at (n,q)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2) and direct maximal cliques at n=2. These examples corroborate rather than prove the unrestricted result.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the all-arity pairwise-commuting tuple census with joint rank distribution and the classification/count of maximal compatible retraction families. An earlier result already classifies individual idempotent Lie endomorphisms by rank and conjugacy; those facts are not claimed anew. Its n+1 orbit decomposition does not determine adjacency between distinct idempotents. Commuting-matrix formulae are not stronger in the Lie category because their idempotent center restrictions need not be exterior-square functorial. The 2019 and 2020 relevant primary texts do not claim tuple or clique classifications. Residual risk is an equivalent published reformulation in general retract semigroups.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-arity formula may be formulated in universal-algebra retract decomposition or Lie-endomorphism semilattice literature under different vocabulary.
The closest prior individual-retraction classification could facilitate a different derivation; novelty here is the full multiway enumerator and classification, not the single-retraction spectrum.
The 2020 representation paper was read in relevant sections rather than every displayed computation.

value.rationale: All-arity clique counts and joint rank spectra quantify mutual compatibility of Lie algebra splittings, not just existence or individual orbit sizes. The Boolean maximal family structure and exact q^(n choose 2 times n) shear multiplier give a natural complete family census over all q,n. The wedge-square AND decomposition is a characteristic coupling invisible to the quotient projection monoid, offering a structural invariant with clear use in enumerating embedded retractions.
